title: SharePoint: FAQ web part that uses Microsoft 365 Copilot to curate FAQs from grounding data
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap status conflict, Restricted Content Discovery controls and Copilot in SharePoint licensing statements are supported. Minor corrections should distinguish the published SharePoint base licence from unpublished feature-specific entitlement and cite the basis for page-wide visibility.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific entitlement for the original FAQ web part is unpublished, so the page labels its licensing model unknown.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included for the SharePoint base entitlement. Replace the first licensing.notes sentence and the first Cost and licensing paragraph with: 'SharePoint access requires a licence that includes SharePoint. Microsoft has not published a licence requirement specific to the original AI FAQ web part.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/sharepoint-online-service-description/sharepoint-online-service-description. Preserve the separate Microsoft 365 Copilot requirement for the Copilot in SharePoint authoring route; do not claim that the base SharePoint licence includes AI authoring.

claims.quote: Searched: '"FAQ" "Copilot in SharePoint" "rate" "Credits"'; read Copilot in SharePoint get-started and returned licensing excerpts. They give task-dependent credit consumption, not a FAQ generation rate.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is enabled through SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the specified site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery by default.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level setting that removes AI entry points, including Copilot in SharePoint.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing setting that's respected. If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.
